thread:
Matt H: seeing a spike of 502s from edge-proxy in us-west2 since ~08:12. ALB health shows targets healthy but responses are connection reset / upstream closed.
Alisha P: can you paste a curl or logs? which service path?
Matt H: reproducer: `curl -v https://edge.example.com/health` -> TLS handshake ok then `* Connection reset by peer`. Request hits proxy pods. logs: `upstream read error: connection reset by peer` from nginx-proxy.
Ben K: curious — last config change? any SG/NACL edits or NAT scaling?
Matt H: no infra changes in last 24h from our side. but deploy-bot shows a canary rollout of edge-proxy v2.3.4 at 08:09:22.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy edge-proxy v2.3.4 started by alisha at 2026-02-15T08:09:22Z.
Alisha P: hmm could be app bug but the pattern looks like transient TCP resets. infra-oncall can you check NAT gateway metrics & conntrack?
infra-oncall: checking now. NAT gw metrics show a short spike in { "allocated_ports": "~64000", "port_exhaustion": "2 short windows", "timeframe": "08:10-08:13" } -> probable source port exhaustion + source-port reuse causing TCP resets. also seeing elevated SNAT errors in VPC flow logs.
SRE Bot: Alert: 502 rate increased 4x in us-west2 between 08:11 and 08:14.
Ben K: that would line up — if SNAT pool runs out some connections get immediate RST/ICMP and the proxy treats that as upstream error. Also saw similar when transiently opening many backend connections per request.
Matt H: the proxy uses persistent upstreams but can spike ephemeral connections during canary due to heavier healthchecks + backend warmups. Could be the canary doubled connection bursts.
Alisha P: quick mitigation options? add more NAT gateways, increase ephemeral port range, or put an egress NAT fleet for the proxy nodes. Which is fastest?
infra-oncall: fastest short-term is to increase ephemeral port range on the NAT instances (if using NAT instances) or add another managed NAT gateway (if using managed NAT) — adding NAT gw in the AZ should relieve exhaustion in ~2-5m. also we can temporarily reduce healthcheck frequency for the canary.
Ben K: also confirm security groups/NACL not blocking return ports — I saw a custom NACL that had a narrow ephemeral range denied for egress in a couple subnets earlier this month. if NACL denies ephemeral ports you'll see asymmetric failures even with NAT.
Matt H: we do have a conservative NACL on the edge-subnet: deny high ports 49152-65535 for ingress (legacy rule). that could be part of it.
Alisha P: ahh. that's probably it — canary increased outbound connection count, and NACL + SNAT exhaustion = dropped flows. Can we amend the NACL to allow ephemeral return?
infra-oncall: updating NACL now to allow ephemeral return (49152-65535) for ingress on the edge-subnet, and spinning up one additional managed NAT gw in us-west2b. executing: `aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abc123 --ingress --rule-number 100 --protocol -1 --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --rule-action allow` (then add rule for high ports).
Matt H: rolled back canary to v2.3.3 as a precaution.
deploy-bot: Rollback: edge-proxy -> v2.3.3 initiated by Matt H at 2026-02-15T08:17:10Z.
infra-oncall: NAT gw added and NACL relaxed. monitoring: allocated_ports back to normal, SNAT errors cleared by 08:25.
Ben K: please follow up with a postmortem note to ops-runbook: ensure ephemeral port rules documented and autoscale NAT capacity when proxy canaries roll out.
Alisha P: created runbook task and will add a canary preflight check for NAT headroom.
Matt H: thanks — after rollback 502s dropped back to baseline. will re-run canary with healthcheck throttle and jitter. :thumbsup:
SRE Bot: Incident cleared at 2026-02-15T08:26:40Z.
